construct: An acquired PIGA mutation impairs glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchor synthesis, preventing complement-regulatory proteins such as CD55 and CD59 from attaching normally to blood-cell surfaces. Loss of these regulators permits complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis and contributes to thrombosis.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Coombs-negative intravascular hemolysis plus unusual-site venous thrombosis and loss of CD55/CD59 on granulocytes identify PNH from an acquired GPI-anchor defect.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Factor V Leiden can explain venous thrombosis, including unusual thrombosis in some patients, but cannot explain intravascular hemolysis or the flow-cytometric loss of CD55/CD59; hereditary spherocytosis likewise cannot explain the clonal GPI-anchor phenotype.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The flow-cytometric loss of two GPI-anchored complement regulators makes an acquired PIGA/GPI-anchor defect uniquely explanatory for both hemolysis and thrombosis.
